evidence_basis: Six indexed capability partitions contain 60 Debian-rootfs oracle identities and one local graphics-experiment identity
accepted_semantic_boundary: The six capability partitions are accepted authority-review units; no object inherits final provider authority from observed location, package ownership or first-generation selection
candidate_source_class_decision: Debian/rootfs and local experiment bytes are reference evidence only; exact Termux-glibc, upstream-generic or project-built candidates require artifact/source/adaptation evidence; protected-world, application-local and application-supplement ownership require an explicit owning-authority exception; native Android requires a proved ABI adapter
validation_trigger: Any proposed object/provider/source binding or authority-domain change
rollback_boundary: No runtime state changed; rollback is removal of the proposed authority record
unresolved: Exact candidate artifacts, source trees, adaptation effects, clean acquisition, object necessity and final provider decisions

evidence_basis: Ten Debian-rootfs oracle identities; Phase B3/B4 record a required NSS/NSPR/security direction including dynamic modules and SQLite support
accepted_semantic_boundary: Security/NSS is a required application capability direction, but its exact external object set and shared-provider source remain open
candidate_source_class_decision: Shared generic provider candidates are preferred for review; automatic application-supplement ownership, protected-world inheritance and Debian-oracle promotion are rejected; exact Termux/upstream/project candidates remain to be compared
validation_trigger: Payload/Electron change; NSS module set change; proposed source or application-supplement exception
rollback_boundary: Rollback reselects the previous accepted shared security provider tuple with its compatible payload
unresolved: Exact package/artifact/source identity, adaptation evidence, complete module set, trust-store policy and rollback validation

evidence_basis: Thirty-six Debian-rootfs oracle identities in the dominant GTK/GLib/GIO/ATK/Cairo/Pango/font/X11 support direction
accepted_semantic_boundary: The GTK GUI group is accepted static capability pressure; package overlap does not authorize one copied deployment tree or final source
candidate_source_class_decision: Compare exact shared Termux-glibc, generic upstream and project-built candidates; Debian bytes remain oracle-only; protected-world and application-supplement ownership are rejected absent an object-specific exception
validation_trigger: GTK/Electron ABI change; X11-versus-Wayland policy change; proposed object/source/provider change
rollback_boundary: Rollback reselects the previous accepted GTK shared-provider composition; application payload and world rollback remain separate
unresolved: Exact object closure, Termux/Android adaptation, X11-only versus Wayland composition, source/build binding and update contract

evidence_basis: One Debian-rootfs oracle libasound identity with direct entrypoint/static capability pressure
accepted_semantic_boundary: ALSA remains a distinct audio capability direction; direct pressure does not by itself establish permanent inclusion or source authority
candidate_source_class_decision: A shared generic ALSA provider is the review class; Debian-oracle promotion and automatic app supplement ownership are rejected; exact Termux/upstream/project candidate comparison is open
validation_trigger: Declared audio requirement, Electron NEEDED set or provider candidate change
rollback_boundary: Rollback removes or reselects the audio capability only with a compatible application composition
unresolved: Capability requirement, exact artifact/source, adaptation, service/device contract and rollback validation

evidence_basis: One Debian-rootfs oracle libudev identity with distinct device-observation pressure
accepted_semantic_boundary: udev remains a distinct device capability direction; observed rootfs supply is not native Android or final generic authority
candidate_source_class_decision: Compare a shared glibc-ABI provider or an explicitly proved native-Android adapter; Debian-oracle promotion, protected-world inheritance and app-supplement fallback are rejected
validation_trigger: Named device-observation requirement, ABI-adapter proposal or provider candidate change
rollback_boundary: Rollback removes or reselects the device capability without changing payload, world or user data
unresolved: Need, exact provider/source, Android integration model, service/socket behavior and rollback validation

evidence_basis: Ten Debian-rootfs oracle identities spanning CUPS, Avahi, D-Bus/systemd and TLS support
accepted_semantic_boundary: Printing is a separate capability direction whose base-runtime inclusion remains rejected until requirement and ownership are accepted
candidate_source_class_decision: Compare exact shared printing-stack candidates only after printing is declared; Debian-oracle promotion, base inheritance and application-supplement fallback are rejected
validation_trigger: Declared printing requirement; CUPS/service/TLS source or provider proposal
rollback_boundary: Rollback removes the optional printing capability and restores the prior application composition
unresolved: Whether printing is required, exact provider/source set, service policy, trust/update boundary and rollback validation

evidence_basis: Two Debian-rootfs oracle identities plus one local graphics-experiment identity; libgbm is static load pressure while Vulkan roots are feature-conditional

candidate_source_class_decision: Exact graphics provider candidates require artifact/source/adaptation and accepted GPU-policy binding; Debian/rootfs and local experiment bytes remain references; no automatic generic, platform or app-supplement promotion
validation_trigger: GPU policy, Mesa/Freedreno source, libgbm ABI or Vulkan feature-set change
rollback_boundary: Rollback restores the previous accepted graphics policy/provider tuple independently of the base application payload
unresolved: Complete libgbm/Mesa/Freedreno source authority, platform-versus-generic ownership, exact conditional set and update/rollback contract
